title: invariant.yaml
description: An API's Invariant configuration. Everything the command needs is here or beside it, so a check gives the same answer on a laptop with no network as it does in CI.

api.description: The API's name: what its runtimes, signed releases and the hosted service call it.

spec.description: Where each contract's OpenAPI document comes from.

current.description: The contract being built: a path to a committed document, or a command that generates one.

command.description: Run through the shell in the repository's root before every check.

currentLabel.description: What the contract being built is called before it is released. Without it the compiled program is named after the day it was built.

released.description: Every contract still served, by label, to its committed document.

identity.description: How a request names the contract it expects. The first strategy that matches decides.

name.description: header: the request header that carries the label.

map.description: urlPrefix: path prefixes to the contract each one means.

label.description: default: the contract a request that names none is on.

description.description: For whoever reads the file; not compiled.

scenarios.description: Requests the full check sends each build, made from each released contract's own document.

generate.description: For a contract with no scenarios written by hand (missing), beside them (always), or not at all (never).

headers.description: Headers every generated request carries, such as a test credential.

build.description: How to stand up builds, so the full check can compare what the old and new builds do.

base.description: A released contract's build, when it is the current code started differently.

command.description: Starts a released contract's build, when not the way the current build is started.

env.description: ${contract} is replaced with the label being built.

healthPath.description: Answers 200 once the server is ready.

contracts.description: A released contract's own build, by label: an environment already running, the image that was released, or the commit it came from.

gate.description: What the release gate does about the things a provider may decide on. Unexplained breaking changes and failed verification always block.

declaredLossy.description: A Change that serves old callers with something lost, and says so.

unmigratableWithActiveConsumers.description: A Change no codemod can apply, while consumers still use what it changes.

retirement.description: When each released contract is deprecated and when it stops being served, by label. The runtime tells that contract's callers on every answer, as Deprecation (RFC 9745) and Sunset (RFC 8594).

deprecated.description: The day this contract was deprecated. A date, or a date and time.

sunset.description: The day this contract stops being served.
